intro.text: Labcorp ® Holdings Inc. is a global leader of innovative and comprehensive laboratory services that provides vital information to help doctors, hospitals, pharmaceutical companies, researchers, and patients make clear and confident decisions. The Company provides insights and accelerates innovations to improve health and improve lives through its unparalleled diagnostics and drug development laboratory capabilities. During 2025, the Company’s nearly 71,000 employees served clients in approximately 100 countries and performed more than 750 million tests for patients around the world. In addition, the Company provided support for more than 85% of the new drugs and therapeutic products approved in 2025 by the FDA.

BLS revenues for the year ended December 31, 2024, were $2,922.6, an increase of 5.3% over revenues of $2,774.2 in the corresponding period in 2023. The increase in revenues was primarily due to organic growth of 4.3% and favorable foreign currency translation of 1.1%.

cor.heading: Cost of Revenues
cor.text: Cost of revenues increased 5.9% for the year ended December 31, 2025, as compared with corresponding period in 2024, and decreased as a percentage of revenues to 71.2% for the year ended December 31, 2025, as compared to 72.1% for the corresponding period in 2024. This decrease was primarily due to operational efficiencies and the impact from revenue growth, including the performance of Invitae.

oi.text: Dx segment operating income was $1,779.9 for the year ended December 31, 2025, an increase of 10.8% from operating income of $1,606.3 in the corresponding period of 2024, and Dx operating margin increased approximately 50 basis points year-over-year. The increase in operating margin was primarily due to increased organic revenue growth, including the performance of Invitae.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text: For the year ended December 31, 2025, interest expense increased 7.6% as compared with the corresponding period in 2024. The increase was primarily due to higher weighted-average interest rates during the year ended December 31, 2025, when compared to the year ended December 31, 2024.

tax.heading: Provision for Income Taxes
tax.text: The decrease in the effective tax rate for the year ended December 31, 2025, as compared with the corresponding period in 2024, was primarily attributable to the release of specific uncertain tax positions.

ocf.heading: Cash Flows from Operating Activities
ocf.text: During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company’s operations provided $1,640.5 of cash as compared to $1,585.8 in 2024. The $54.7 increase in net cash provided from operations in 2025, as compared with the corresponding 2024 period, was primarily due to higher cash earnings, partially offset by working capital timing.

wc.text: • Annual cash flows, on a debt-free basis, arising from future revenues and profitability, working capital changes, capital spending and income taxes for at least a five-year forecast period.

capex.text: Capital expenditures were $434.5 and $489.9 for the years ended December 31, 2025, and 2024, respectively. Capital expenditures in 2025 were 3.1% of revenues, primarily in connection with projects to support growth in the Company’s core businesses. The Company expects this level of spending to increase in 2026 to 4.0%, primarily in connection with projects to support growth in the Company’s core businesses, facility expansion and updates, projects related to its LaunchPad initiative, and further acquisition integration initiatives.

net sales.heading: Revenues
net sales.text:
Dx revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025, were $10,876.5, an increase of 7.2% compared to revenues of $10,144.3 in the corresponding period in 2024. The increase was primarily due to organic revenue of 4.1% and acquisitions, net of divestitures of 3.2%, partially offset by unfavorable foreign currency translation of 0.1%.

Dx total volume, measured by requisitions, increased by 3.7%, as organic volume increased by 2.2% and acquisition volume, net of divestitures, contributed 1.5%. Price/mix increased by 3.5% due to organic growth of 1.9% and acquisitions, net of divestitures, of 1.7%, partially offset by unfavorable foreign currency translation of 0.1%.

BLS revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025, were $3,098.2, an increase of 6.0% over revenues of $2,922.6 in the corresponding period in 2024. The increase in revenues was primarily due to organic growth of 4.0% and favorable foreign currency translation of 2.0%.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
